sermon.title: To Cover or Not to Cover Part 1
sermon.series: To Cover or Not to Cover
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “To Cover or Not to Cover Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer begins a study of praying and prophesying with the head covered or uncovered in 1 Corinthians 11. Before the topic itself, he stresses following Christ rather than other people or man-made traditions, then lays out the chain of command in 1 Corinthians 11:3. He then starts working through the verses about men and women praying and prophesying, and the series continues in Part 2.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. In the sermon he cites “1 Chronicles 25:4” for the words about David separating people to prophesy; in the NKJV that wording is in 1 Chronicles 25:1, and Heman’s fourteen sons and three daughters are in 1 Chronicles 25:5–6, so those passages are shown here. His words are unchanged. Some of the sermon refers to things on the screen, such as pictures and a scarf and hat he is wearing, which are not visible in the transcript.

chunks.section_question: Who should Christians follow: Jesus or church leaders?
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul begins by saying to follow him as he follows Christ, so we are not to follow other religious leaders, famous preachers or any church movement, but Jesus Christ. He says Jesus only taught and lived by the Word of God, always did the will of the Father, and that a preacher should preach the Scriptures, not their opinion or some church doctrine.
chunks.text:
Okay, now Paul opens with this statement. He says, “Be you followers, imitators of me, even as I also am of Christ.” Now it’s important that he introduces this subject this way, because when he comes to the conclusion you’re going to need this introductory subject. Okay, he says be followers of me as I follow Christ. In other words, we almost follow who? Christ. And people who follow Christ. Yes. My covering is slipping. I need [unclear]. Now let’s don’t get carried away.

In other words, we’re not to follow Muhammad, we’re not to follow Joseph Smith, we’re not to follow the Pope, we’re not to follow Billy Graham, we’re not to follow Oral Roberts or Joel Osteen or Rick Warren, or the emergent church or the seeker-friendly church or the Pentecostal church or the Baptist church or whatever. We are to follow who? Jesus Christ. And he’s hitting a very important issue before he gets into this subject. We get our eyes off Christ and we get our eyes on other things, and we have problems. Could that be an amen? And said, “I only do what I see Christ do. I only do what Jesus teach. You follow me as I follow Him, and if I don’t follow Jesus, don’t follow me,” is what he’s saying. Now Jesus did no sin.

Wow, that sure beats all these other guys I listed. Jesus only taught and lived by the Word of God. He taught the Scriptures; He didn’t teach other books. Remember, there were books there. Homer was there, Greek and Roman mythology books were there, Aristotle was there, Socrates was there, the Jewish book of traditions was there. He never taught any of that. He taught what? The Scriptures. He said follow me as I follow Christ. How many, you know, a preacher should be preaching the Scriptures, not their opinion or some church doctrine. See, he’s setting this thing up for a real good answer. Jesus always followed and did the will of the Father, always. You see, Jesus went to the synagogue every Saturday. I’ll [unclear]. This is how these women do that. There we go. Now I won’t fall off. Aren’t I cute? See, Jesus did the will of the Father. He went to the synagogue. He worked till He was 30 years old and went into the ministry. He actually worked; He was a carpenter. He actually held a job, just like the Bible tells us to. Jesus laid down His life and He picked it up again and lived again. Jesus said, “No greater love hath any man than he lays down his life for his friend.” Jesus said, “You are my friends if you do what I ask you to do.”

chunks.section_question: How did Jesus’ apostles live, and why does Paul praise the Corinthians?
chunks.short_answer: He says there is no record of the apostles Jesus taught directly, except Judas, misusing church money, committing sexual immorality, idolatry, complaining or dividing, and that they kept serving God until they died. He says we need to follow people who follow Jesus, and that Paul honors the Corinthians for keeping his teachings even though they were “crude,” because when he corrected them, they changed.
chunks.text:
And we’re to lay down our life for our friend. Jesus, isn’t that right? See, follow Jesus. Forget these other people; follow Jesus. Jesus taught directly 14 apostles. He encountered them and sent them to teach His Word. And there is no record of any of these apostles that He directly taught, except Judas who was picked for that, there’s no record of these guys misusing church money, these guys committing sexual immorality, whether it was incest, homosexuality, adultery or fornication. No record; they didn’t do it. There’s no record of them using extortion because of the position in the church, getting people to do things for them and give them things. There’s no record of them committing idolatry. There’s no record of them complaining. There’s no record of them dividing. Are you there? See, when we follow Jesus we’ll all be on the same track.

See, there’s no record of them quitting. They didn’t give up; they didn’t have nervous breakdowns and all this stuff. They kept preaching and serving God all the days of their life till their hearts stopped or they were killed. They martyred and died, isn’t that right? They never needed a sabbatical to get their head together. These guys were powerful. That’s the kind of people Jesus makes. How many, you know, we need to be following Jesus, and we need to be following people that are following Jesus. And so this is very important. Now Paul then goes in to honor them for changing wrong beliefs and wrong behavior when he taught them proper Bible tradition, Bible rules, Bible truths.

And he says, “I praise you, brethren, that you remember me in all things and keep the ordinances,” the traditions, the customs, the rules, the teachings, “as I delivered them to you.” And as crude as this church was, with their division, their sexual immorality, their idolatry, their faith in men instead of the power of God, and not seeking the high prize of God, and the complaining when Paul would come and correct them and teach them, they would change, and he honored them for it. I mean, that’s a powerful thing. I mean, we should have that kind of heart. You know, we might have some errors, but goodness, when we hear truth, let’s change. See, he’s setting this up good for this interesting topic.

chunks.section_question: What man-made traditions does the Bible warn against?
chunks.short_answer: He says the Bible shows several traditions not to follow: the tradition of the elders (leaders making up their own rules), the traditions of men, being captured through philosophy and vain deceit, keeping your own tradition over the commandment of God, and the traditions of your religious or family fathers. He says “we will take tradition over the Word of God, and it nullifies and neutralizes the Word of God.”
chunks.text:
Then he goes and hits another subject, the chain of command. Before he gets into the topic, but before we get there, there are five traditions in the Bible, customs, and we want to hit those so you know what not to follow. In Mark 7:5, the tradition of the elders, the Sanhedrin, the Jewish civil leaders. They made up their own laws: you got to, if you’re going to eat, you got to have a ceremonial washing of the hands. See, traditions of the leaders. Some people will die for church leaders that make up their own rules, and they’re not in the Bible. Could that be true? That is true. In fact, we will take tradition over the Word of God, and it nullifies and neutralizes the Word of God.

The second area of traditions is in Mark 7:8, traditions of men, like the washing of pots and cups and the Sabbath day journey and many other things that you do. The tradition of men is not only in the church, but it’s also in the secular world. Colossians 2:8, “Beware lest any man spoil you.” The word “spoil” means capture you, like a bandit, you know. They come and they rob you and they capture, they overpower you and they take what you have. He says beware lest any man capture you through philosophy. They’re going to capture your mind. Philosophy is the way of life and values that you live by. They capture you through philosophy, they capture you through vain, fruitless deceit; they’re actually deceiving you, “and after the tradition of men,” you see, the rules, the customs of men, “after the rudiments,” the principles, “of this world and not after Christ.” And we got to be careful what rules we’re following. Could that be true? What customs? What traditions?

Now the third one, Mark 7:9, “You full well reject the commandment of God that you may keep your own tradition.” We’re not just happy with following the church leaders’ nonsense and people of the world; we come up with our own. “This is what I believe,” and it hurts us, it can destroy our life, and it robs us of the things of Christ. And then number four, Galatians 1:14, “I, Paul, profited in the Jewish religion above my equals in my own nation.” You know, we get in our little religion, whether it’s Baptist or Presbyterian or Lutheran or whatever, or Catholic, and man, we want to be, you know, the best in that group, and we do everything they say to try to, you know, be recognized. That’s the real Baptist, that’s the real Methodist, that’s the real Pentecostal, or whatever. Man, I’m “being more zealous of the traditions of my fathers,” religious fathers and also family fathers. You know, there’s people that follow the traditions of their family handed down, even if it goes against the Word of God.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then the Pharisees and scribes asked Him, “Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashed hands?”
For laying aside the commandment of God, you hold the tradition of men—the washing of pitchers and cups, and many other such things you do.”
Beware lest anyone cheat you through philosophy and empty deceit, according to the tradition of men, according to the basic principles of the world, and not according to Christ.
He said to them, “All too well you reject the commandment of God, that you may keep your tradition.
And I advanced in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries in my own nation, being more exceedingly zealous for the traditions of my fathers.

chunks.section_question: Which traditions does the Bible tell Christians to keep?
chunks.short_answer: He says the real traditions are what the apostles taught: in 2 Thessalonians 2:15 Paul says to hold the traditions taught by word or by epistle, which he says shows the epistles were Scripture. He says we are to withdraw from those who come up with their own man-made doctrines, and follow “Bible, Jesus, apostle traditions.”
chunks.text:
And he says this is not the ordinances, the traditions I’m talking about. These are the ordinance and tradition that will take you away from truth, take you away from God, and weaken you. I want you to follow the real traditions. 2 Thessalonians 2:15, “Hold the traditions which you have been taught, whether by word,” or the Bible Scriptures, “or by our epistles.” Now in this verse he is declaring that the epistles written by Peter, Paul, John and James were Scripture. You understand that? Hallelujah. So when these people argue about the canonization of the Bible and all that, they’re arguing fruitlessly. Paul recognized these epistles as what? Scripture. Why? They got it straight from God; they got their doctrines from Jesus Christ, and the Bible tells us to follow the apostles’ doctrines and Christ’s doctrines, no one else.

Number two, in 2 Thessalonians 3:6, the second part of this number five tradition: “Withdraw from brothers that walk disorderly.” Well, how do we know they walk disorderly? Because they don’t walk after the tradition which he “received of us.” He’s not following us as we follow Christ. Got it? He’s coming up with his own man-made doctrines. And so that’s what he’s saying: don’t follow those other ordinances, those other customs, those other traditions; follow Bible, Jesus, apostle traditions.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore, brethren, stand fast and hold the traditions which you were taught, whether by word or our epistle.
But we command you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you withdraw from every brother who walks disorderly and not according to the tradition which he received from us.

chunks.section_question: What is God’s chain of command in 1 Corinthians 11:3?
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul reminds them of the chain of leadership: the head of every man is Christ, the head of the woman is the husband, and the head of Christ is God. He says “No man has authority over another woman,” and that this shows Jesus is under the authority of God, while Jesus has all power in heaven and earth and the others have only delegated authority.
chunks.text:
Now verse 3, he comes up and he makes this powerful statement. He’s going to remind them of the chain of command, of the chain of leadership. Now you need to get this in your cranial vacuum. This is God’s chain of leadership. “The head of every man is” what? Jesus Christ. “The head of every woman is the,” and what’s the word for man there? Husband. Say it: husband. No man has authority over another woman. It’s husband. “The head of Christ is God.” Head is Christ, and the head of the woman is the man, and the head of Christ is who? God.

These people that want to say Jesus only and all that: it plainly says Jesus is under the leadership, the authority, of who? God. When Stephen saw the heavens open, he saw Jesus standing on the right hand of the glory of who? God. See, the Godhead is plural, and there’s an order of authority, and if you follow here with me, Jesus is over everything. Didn’t He say, “All power in heaven and earth has been given unto Me”? See, He’s not only the head of the man, He’s the head of everything, and as you follow to the right there, He’s the head of the angels. The angels have delegated authority. Those dotted lines are delegated authority over the church, and over Satan, coming down through the church, and over civil authorities, the husband, the wife and kids. They can only do what Jesus gives them permission to do. Amen.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, the head of woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.

But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God, and said, “Look! I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God!”
And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth.

chunks.section_question: Who has authority over the church, the husband and the wife?
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus has direct authority over civil governments, the church and the wife, and that pastors are only delegated. He says the wife has two heads, the husband as a delegated authority and Jesus as her direct authority, so if a husband asks her to do something that violates the authority of Christ, she cannot do it.
chunks.text:
And then you see that He is the direct authority over civil governments. Daniel says the Most High rules in the kingdoms of men and gives it to whomsoever He will. Satan is not ruling in the kingdoms of men; the Bible says who is? God Himself, the Most High. And a lot of people got this teaching all wrong. Secondly, He’s over the church. The Bible says He’s the head of the body, the church, doesn’t He? He’s the real pastor. Us preachers are just delegated, you know, blabbermouths. Really, Jesus is the real power, He’s the real Shepherd. And so when a pastor violates the customs, traditions and rules of Christ, we’re not to follow them, because our real leader is who? Jesus Christ. And then of course we see Him here over the husband, and He has direct authority over the wife. See, the wife has two heads: the husband is a delegated authority, but Jesus is their direct authority. And when a husband asks the wife to do something that violates the authority of Christ, she can’t do that, saying “I got to be submissive.” Are you there, church? Hallelujah. Yeah.

Now to show you that women knew that were married who their head was, who their leader was, remember Elizabeth: Zachariah and Elizabeth, who had John the Baptist. Mary came to visit Elizabeth, and Elizabeth looks at her and says, “Why is it that the mother of my Lord”? Now who was Mary? The mother of Jesus. See, Elizabeth knew who her Lord was, the real authority: “that the mother of my Lord should come to me.” All right, you got to understand, and you got to get this chain of command in you so we don’t get messed up here. All right, we come down to the kids. “Permit all children to come unto Me.”

They’re both leaders, and we’ll show you that more clearly. Now let me get my babushka back on; it keeps falling off up here. “Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonors his head.” Yikes, and get this thing off of me.

faqs.question: What question does this message take up?
faqs.answer: Whether we pray and prophesy with our head covered or uncovered. He says “Paul’s going to hit this thing today,” starting with a chain of command, and he is going to answer it from 1 Corinthians 11.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonors his head.

faqs.question: Why does Paul start by saying “be followers of me”?
faqs.answer: He says it is important because when Paul comes to his conclusion, “you’re going to need this introductory subject.” The point is to follow Christ, and people who follow Christ.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Imitate me, just as I also imitate Christ.

faqs.question: Did Jesus teach anything besides the Scriptures?
faqs.answer: He says no. Jesus only taught the Scriptures and “didn’t teach other books,” even though books of Greek and Roman mythology, philosophers and Jewish traditions were available. He says a preacher should be preaching the Scriptures, not their opinion or some church doctrine.

faqs.question: Did the apostles ever quit or burn out?
faqs.answer: He says there is no record of them quitting, giving up, or having nervous breakdowns. They kept preaching and serving God all the days of their lives, “till their hearts stopped or they were killed.”

faqs.question: How did the Corinthians respond when Paul corrected them?
faqs.answer: He says that although they were crude, with division, sexual immorality and idolatry, they would change when Paul corrected and taught them, and he honored them for it. “When we hear truth, let’s change.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now I praise you, brethren, that you remember me in all things and keep the traditions just as I delivered them to you.

faqs.question: What does Colossians 2:8 mean by “capture you through philosophy”?
faqs.answer: He says “spoil” means capture you like a bandit, and that philosophy is the way of life and values that you live by. They capture your mind through philosophy and “vain, fruitless deceit.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Beware lest anyone cheat you through philosophy and empty deceit, according to the tradition of men, according to the basic principles of the world, and not according to Christ.

faqs.question: Does Paul treat the apostles’ letters as Scripture?
faqs.answer: He says that in 2 Thessalonians 2:15 Paul is declaring that the epistles written by Peter, Paul, John and James were Scripture. He says that is why arguing about canonization of the Bible is fruitless.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore, brethren, stand fast and hold the traditions which you were taught, whether by word or our epistle.

faqs.question: Is Jesus under the authority of God?
faqs.answer: He says it plainly says Jesus is under the leadership and authority of God, and that Stephen saw Jesus standing at the right hand of the glory of God. He says the Godhead is plural, with an order of authority.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God, and said, “Look! I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God!”

faqs.question: Does the church have authority over the elements?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus has direct authority over the elements, which is why He could say “Peace, be still” and heal the sick. The church can do these things only as Jesus gives us permission.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then He arose and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace, be still!” And the wind ceased and there was a great calm.

faqs.question: Is Paul talking about every woman or every wife?
faqs.answer: He asks whether the word there is “every woman” or “every wife,” and says Paul is talking about husband and wife, “not talking about single women at all.” Yet these churches interpret it to mean women have to wear something on their head.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for that is one and the same as if her head were shaved.

faqs.question: Will Jesus hear the prayer of a woman who is not covered?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus does not care where the covering is, and he asks, “He ain’t going to hear my prayer because I don’t have a covering? No.”

faqs.question: Doesn’t the Bible say women must keep silent in church?
faqs.answer: He raises this objection and answers that here Paul says women can pray and prophesy, and asks how you prophesy “with your mouth shut.” He says Paul is establishing that women can be involved in the church.

faqs.question: Can you prophesy with music and singing?
faqs.answer: He says the word prophecy in 1 Chronicles 25 is the same as the other words, except it means we sing and play musical instruments by the inspiration and anointing of the Spirit. We can edify and prophesy with our instrument without song and with instruments with song.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Moreover David and the captains of the army separated for the service some of the sons of Asaph, of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, stringed instruments, and cymbals. And the number of the skilled men performing their service was:

faqs.question: Why does Paul say a man should not cover his head?
faqs.answer: He says Paul said it was a shame for a man to pray or prophesy with something on his head, yet in the Bible Aaron and his sons had to have something on their head, a miter or cap. He says Paul knows this.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And Moses said to Aaron, and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons, “Do not uncover your heads nor tear your clothes, lest you die, and wrath come upon all the people. But let your brethren, the whole house of Israel, bewail the burning which the LORD has kindled.

faqs.question: What is our covering according to Psalm 140?
faqs.answer: He quotes “Lord, You have covered my head in the day of battle” and says that covering points to having the Lord Jesus Christ and His authority covering us.

scriptures.text_nkjv: O GOD the Lord, the strength of my salvation, You have covered my head in the day of battle.
